questions.question: Why should you not make sudden stops in front of large trucks and buses?

options.text: Small vehicle drivers cannot see large trucks and buses in their rearview mirrors.
Large trucks and buses need longer distances to stop because of their size and weight.
Large trucks and buses travel faster than small vehicles.

questions.correctAnswerText: Large trucks and buses need longer distances to stop because of their size and weight.
questions.explanation: Large vehicles need more distance to stop than smaller vehicles. If you stop suddenly in front of a large vehicle, the driver may not have enough time to stop and could hit you.

questions.question: If your vehicle breaks down, what should you do?

options.text: Signal and move to the slow lane.
Stop in your lane and turn on your hazard lights.
Turn on your hazard lights and drive off the road.

questions.correctAnswerText: Turn on your hazard lights and drive off the road.
questions.explanation: Get your vehicle off the road and away from traffic if you can. Turn on your hazard lights so other drivers can see that you are having trouble.

questions.question: On a slippery road, how far should you stay behind the car ahead?
questions.explanation: You need more distance to stop on a slippery road than on a dry road. Keep a larger distance between your vehicle and the car ahead when driving on slippery roads.

questions.question: When driving in fog, which headlights should you use?
questions.explanation: Use low beam headlights in fog, rain, or snow. High beams reflect off these conditions and make it harder to see.

questions.question: What does a solid yellow arrow on a traffic signal mean?

options.text: Speed up to make the turn before the light changes.
You do not need to signal your turn.
Get ready to stop and let oncoming traffic pass.

questions.correctAnswerText: Get ready to stop and let oncoming traffic pass.
questions.explanation: A solid yellow arrow means the green arrow protection is ending. If you are turning in that direction, prepare to stop and yield to oncoming traffic.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?
questions.explanation: This yellow warning sign tells you a steep hill is coming. Slow down and shift to a lower gear to control your speed and protect your brakes.

questions.question: What are blind spots?

options.text: Spots in your vision when you are tired.
Areas you cannot see in your mirrors.

questions.correctAnswerText: Areas you cannot see in your mirrors.
questions.explanation: When changing lanes, look over your shoulder to check for vehicles near the rear corners of your car. These hidden areas are called blind spots because mirrors cannot show them.

questions.question: What can reduce blood alcohol content (BAC)?
questions.explanation: Only time removes alcohol and its effects from your body.

questions.question: After drinking several beers, how long until the effects wear off?
questions.explanation: Your body needs time to remove alcohol. Coffee, exercise, or cold showers will not speed this up. It takes about one hour for your body to process one drink.

questions.question: Where should children age 12 and under sit in a vehicle with airbags?

options.text: The bed of a pickup truck.

questions.explanation: Airbags can injure young children. Children age 12 or under should always sit in the back seat of a vehicle with airbags.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?
questions.explanation: A triangle-shaped sign pointing down means yield. Slow down when you see this sign. Stop if you need to. If you stop, do so at the marked stop line.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: You must come to a complete stop.

questions.correctAnswerText: You must come to a complete stop.
questions.explanation: An 8-sided sign always means stop. You must come to a complete stop at the marked stop line. Only go when it is safe. If there is no stop line, stop before the crosswalk. If there is no crosswalk, stop before the intersection.

questions.question: You should yield to a pedestrian:

options.text: Only if they are in a crosswalk.
At all times, even if the pedestrian is not obeying traffic laws.
Only if the traffic lights are in the pedestrian's favor.

questions.correctAnswerText: At all times, even if the pedestrian is not obeying traffic laws.
questions.explanation: Always watch for pedestrians near your vehicle. Do everything you can to avoid hitting a pedestrian, no matter the situation.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?
questions.explanation: A round yellow sign means a railroad crossing is ahead.

questions.question: If a traffic signal light is green and a police officer signals for you to stop, you should:

options.text: Do what the vehicle in front of you does.

questions.explanation: Always obey a police officer's instructions, even if they go against traffic signals, signs, or road markings.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Drive with caution and be ready to stop.
You must come to a complete stop.

questions.correctAnswerText: You must come to a complete stop.
questions.explanation: A stop sign is the only 8-sided sign on the road. You must come to a complete stop. Do not go until the intersection is clear and you can safely pass through.

questions.question: If the roadway is wet or icy, you should:
questions.explanation: Slow down on wet or icy roads. Your tires will not grip the road as well in these conditions.

questions.question: If you are driving and you see animals standing near the roadway:

options.text: Speed up to scare them away.
Slow down and proceed with caution.
Quickly swerve into the next lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down and proceed with caution.
questions.explanation: Slow down and be careful if you see animals near the road. They may suddenly move or change direction. There may also be more animals you cannot see.

questions.question: If you approach a stopped school bus that has its lights flashing and signal arm extended, you should:

options.text: Proceed at 15 mph if no children are present.
Proceed at normal speed, but watch for children.

questions.explanation: You must stop when a school bus has flashing lights and an extended stop arm. Stay stopped until the arm is pulled back and the bus moves. This rule applies whether you are behind the bus or across from it.

questions.question: To help others see you when daylight begins to fade, you should use your:
questions.explanation: Turn on your low beam headlights as it gets dark. Only use high beams when no other drivers are nearby.

questions.question: Before you start the car, you should:

options.text: Make sure all passengers buckle their safety belts.

questions.explanation: Make a habit of buckling your safety belt before you start the car. Make sure all passengers buckle theirs too.

questions.question: When a railroad crossing gate starts to lower, you should:

options.text: Speed up and cross the tracks before the gate closes.

questions.explanation: You must stop at a railroad crossing when the gate is lowering. It is not safe to do anything else.

questions.question: To see better in rain or fog, drivers should use:
questions.explanation: Use low beam headlights in rain, snow, sleet, or fog. High beams reflect off water and snow back into your eyes, making it harder to see.

questions.question: You must yield to a pedestrian with a white cane or guide dog:

options.text: Only when the guide dog is leading them across the street.
Only if a crossing guard is present.

questions.explanation: Always give the right-of-way to pedestrians using guide dogs or white canes.

questions.question: When a school bus ahead on your side has red lights flashing, you must:

options.text: Slow down to no faster than 10 mph.
Stop until the lights stop flashing.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop until the lights stop flashing.
questions.explanation: Flashing red lights on a school bus mean it is loading or unloading students. You must stop and wait until the lights stop flashing. Never pass a school bus that is picking up or dropping off students.

questions.question: There is no crosswalk and you see a pedestrian crossing your lane. You should:

options.text: Make eye contact and then pass the pedestrian.
Slow down as you pass the pedestrian.
Stop and let the pedestrian finish crossing.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop and let the pedestrian finish crossing.
questions.explanation: You must yield to pedestrians crossing your lane, even if there is no crosswalk. Let them finish crossing safely.

questions.question: As alcohol in your blood increases, you become:
questions.explanation: Blood alcohol concentration (BAC) measures how much alcohol is in your blood. The higher your BAC, the more impaired you are.

questions.question: Before driving after taking medicine, you should:

options.text: Ask your doctor about how it affects driving.
Open your window and drive slower.

questions.correctAnswerText: Ask your doctor about how it affects driving.
questions.explanation: Medicine, both prescription and over-the-counter, can make it unsafe to drive. Talk to your doctor or pharmacist before driving if you take any medicine.

questions.question: Which statement is true?

options.text: Use cruise control near railroad crossings to keep a steady speed.
You must stop at a railroad crossing when a flagger or stop sign tells you to.
You have the right-of-way at railroad crossings and do not need to stop.

questions.correctAnswerText: You must stop at a railroad crossing when a flagger or stop sign tells you to.
questions.explanation: You must stop at a railroad crossing when directed by a flagger, stop sign, or warning signal. Drive carefully around railroad tracks.

questions.question: Mississippi law requires headlights to be on:

options.text: When the temperature drops below freezing.

questions.explanation: Mississippi law requires headlights on between sunset and sunrise. Use low beams when you are within 500 feet of another vehicle ahead or coming toward you.
